note: Readability rule for the SEN0401 exam texts (owner point 5 and the plain-wording part of point 4, 2026-11-02). Data only: no question and no answer. The numbers 60 and 25 are the lineage agent's rule from the owner's point and are not to be changed. v1.1.0 (owner redesign 2026-11-02): only R3 is replaced; R1, R2, R4, R5, R6 and the 60 and 25 word limits are as in v1.0.0.

R1.label: stem length
R1.text: A stem (the question text without code listings and without the answer-format line) has at most max_stem_words words.

R2.label: no tips or glossary inside a stem
R2.text: No stem contains the word Tips (any case, whole word) or a glossary sentence of the form 'term: meaning'. On the paper a paragraph that starts with 'Tips' under a question counts against that question.

R3.label: one short tip under the stem
R3.text: A stem that needs a tip (its item says so) is followed on the question page by exactly ONE tip line that starts with 'Tip:' and has at most max_tip_words words after the prefix. There is no tips page, no 'see tip' reference, no second tip line and no tip inside the stem. A tip on a stem that needs none is allowed if it obeys the same limits. Replaces the v1.0.0 R3 (named tips on a tips page).

R4.label: answer-format line
R4.text: Every answer-format line has at most max_format_words words, starts with one of the verbs, names the unit in words when the item has a unit, and contains none of the forbidden phrases unless the phrase is explained on the spot (followed at once by a bracket or by 'means' or 'that is').

R5.label: direction length
R5.text: Every direction sentence of the cover (all paragraphs before the first Question heading, tables and footers left out) has at most max_direction_words words.

R6.label: abbreviations spelled out
R6.text: Every abbreviation is spelled out at its first use (reading order: cover, questions, tips), as 'words (ABBR)' or 'ABBR (words)'. An abbreviation is a token of two or more capital letters, a camel-case token with two capitals, a lower-case token with a capital inside (such as kB), or a key of an item's own abbreviations list.
